svg.title: Each generation of a language model agent leaps further. At human step size, a human reads about a third of the leaps. On a smooth path, reading a leap costs about the square root of its length
svg.desc: Six panels in two rows of three generations (generation 1, generation 2, generation 3). At each step of a language model agent, a jagged ball, pale at its center with its mass out along its spikes, shows the distribution of next steps that the language model and its harness induce, and each leap is one draw from it. Each generation is a new model whose distribution frontier labs have stretched in its weights, so leap length grows by 1.4 times each generation (32.5, 45.5, 63.7 units) while the human's budget stays at six small red balls. Top row ('the human falls behind'): checking one draw takes 3, then 4, then 6 red balls, so the human covers two of six leaps in generation 1, one and a half of four leaps in generation 2, and one of three leaps in generation 3. Past that point the agent turns sharply (at least 48 degrees) and scatters to different parts of the dashed runs region (middle-right, upper-left, and bottom-center), missing the goal ring. Bottom row ('the human keeps up'): every turn stays under 6 degrees along the held plan band, checkpoints carry over via dashed arrows into building blocks that bend the next generation's distribution toward the goal, and the agent reaches the goal ring in 6, then 4, then 3 leaps. Reading a leap still costs a little more each generation, but less than the leap grows: six red balls read six leaps in generation 1, five read four in generation 2, and four read three in generation 3, with two balls on the first leap in generations 2 and 3. The human's total falls as the agent's reach grows.
